# Approved runtime components

Node packages provisioned into the collab-msg service must match the versions approved
here. This list is the source of truth for the platform release gate; `package.json`
tracks the allowed ranges.

The service stays on the **ws 7.x** major line this cycle (the 8.x migration is deferred —
it is a breaking API change tracked separately). Offline copies of the upstream advisories
the approvals reference are under `/opt/advisories`; packages resolve from the internal
registry mirror (see `.npmrc`).

| Component | Package | Approved (floor) | Line | Notes                                                                              |
|-----------|---------|------------------|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ws        | ws      | 7.5.10           | 7.x  | Same-branch patch floor per the upstream advisory (see `/opt/advisories`).         |

The collab-msg server accepts external WebSocket handshakes (`server.js` binds all
interfaces), so the approved floor for the 7.x line is **7.5.10** — the patch the ws
maintainers released on the 7.x branch. The `7.5.9` build recorded in the historical
`deploy/package-lock.legacy.json` predates that patch and is below the approved floor;
provision `7.5.10` (or a higher approved 7.x patch) when restoring the service.
---
# collab-msg

Collaboration message service for the platform. A WebSocket relay that accepts client
connections and relays chat frames between participants in a room.

## Layout

- `server.js` — the service entry (`npm start`): opens the WebSocket relay and echoes
  each client's frames back to it.
- `client.js` — a small connect + send probe used by the round-trip check.
- `bin/roundtrip.sh` — launcher: starts the relay and runs one connection + message
  round-trip, printing a `ROUNDTRIP` line.
- `ops/APPROVED-COMPONENTS.md` — the approved runtime component versions for the service.
- `deploy/package-lock.legacy.json` — snapshot of the pinned set the previous box shipped.
- `.npmrc` — points npm at the internal registry mirror.

## Running

Install the WebSocket dependency and run the relay:

```
npm install            # restores dependencies from the internal registry
npm start              # or: bin/roundtrip.sh
```

`bin/roundtrip.sh` prints a `ROUNDTRIP` line once a client connects and its message is
relayed back.

/opt/advisories: ws-GHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q.html --- == /opt/advisories/ws-GHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q.html ws Security Advisory

ws Security Advisory

ws is a simple to use, blazing fast, and thoroughly tested WebSocket client and server implementation for Node.js. The advisory below concerns servers that accept WebSocket handshakes from untrusted clients; a server that upgrades incoming HTTP requests with ws inherits the behaviour of the installed version.

CVE-2024-37890: DoS when handling a request with many HTTP headers

AdvisoryGHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q
CVECVE-2024-37890
Packagews (npm)
SeverityHigh
Affected versions< 5.2.4; >= 6.0.0 < 6.2.3; >= 7.0.0 < 7.5.10; >= 8.0.0 < 8.17.1
Patched versions5.2.4, 6.2.3, 7.5.10, 8.17.1

Description

A request with a number of headers exceeding the server.maxHeadersCount threshold could be used to crash a ws server. The vulnerability affects servers that use ws to accept WebSocket connections (the server role); a client-only use of ws is not affected. Any deployment that upgrades incoming handshakes from untrusted peers with an affected ws release, without a header limit configured, is exposed.

Fix and backports

The fix was released on every maintained line, so a project does not need a major version bump to take it. The patched versions are 5.2.4, 6.2.3, 7.5.10 and 8.17.1. Projects that must stay on the 7.x line should move to 7.5.10, the backported patch for that branch; 7.5.9 and earlier 7.x releases remain affected.

Mitigation

Move to a patched release on your line (7.x → 7.5.10). If upgrading is not immediately possible, the number of allowed headers can be limited with the --max-http-header-size=size Node flag or by setting server.maxHeadersCount to a non-zero value on the HTTP server backing the WebSocket server. The patched-version floor for the 7.x line is 7.5.10; the same-branch patch avoids the breaking API changes of the 8.x line.
